finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.assumptions: The function _88MPH is called recursively with stationName as an argument, and stationName is derived from user input or an untrusted source.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the entire function for any system or exec calls that could use the variable stationName as part of an OS command. No such calls exist; stationName is only passed as an argument to the same function. The function merely constructs a stack of station names and performs arithmetic on battery values. Since there is no OS command execution, the CWE-78 claim is invalid.

finding.title: Buffer Overflow
finding.assumptions: The function _88MPH is called recursively with stationName as an argument, and stationName is derived from user input or an untrusted source.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the code for any fixed-size buffers or array accesses that could overflow. The variable `stationName` is a `std::string` and is only used as an argument to the recursive call and as a key in an `unordered_map`. `std::string` manages its own dynamic memory, so no overflow can occur from assigning a long string. The map lookup `mapOfChargingStations[startingLocation]` uses `operator[]`, which will insert a new entry if the key is missing, but this also does not overflow any buffer. No other code in the fragment performs a raw memory copy or array indexing based on `stationName`. Therefore the reported buffer overflow cannot happen in this code fragment.

finding.title: Integer Overflow or Wraparound
finding.assumptions: currentDistance is derived from user input or an untrusted source.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the operation on line 37 uses double arithmetic (currentDistance * 0.346) rather than integer arithmetic, so no integer overflow or wraparound can occur. Verified that currentDistance is a double field of the edge struct accessed via mapOfChargingStations[startingLocation] on line 32, which is not an integer type. No additional checks or constraints are needed to prevent overflow in this context.
